questions.stem: An IT team needs to install Windows 11 on 200 laptops shipped to remote employees worldwide. The employees should turn the laptop on and have everything configured automatically, including domain join and email. Which install method fits BEST?

choices.text: Clean install with a bootable USB drive at each site
PXE boot from the local network
Zero-touch deployment
Repair installation

questions.explanation: Zero-touch deployment automates the entire install + configuration so a remote user can open the laptop and be productive without intervention.
questions.trap: PXE boot also automates the install but requires the device to be on the local corporate LAN with a PXE server. Won't help a remote user.

questions.stem: A technician wants to install Windows 11 on a system that currently uses an MBR-partitioned drive with legacy BIOS. The installer reports a partitioning incompatibility. What is the MOST likely cause?

choices.text: MBR is limited to 2 TB partitions and the drive is larger
Windows 11 requires UEFI and GPT, which the system does not have
MBR does not support 64-bit operating systems
Secure Boot is enabled but the disk uses legacy partitions

questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires UEFI BIOS (and therefore a GPT-partitioned drive) along with Secure Boot. Legacy BIOS + MBR will fail.
questions.trap: (a) sounds plausible but the issue is the BIOS/partition style, not necessarily the drive size.

questions.stem: A user has a critical Windows 10 system that boots but applications crash and some OS files appear corrupt. They want to fix the OS without losing their installed programs and data. What should the technician perform?

choices.text: Clean install
Repair installation
Quick format and reinstall
Full format and reinstall

questions.explanation: A repair installation overwrites OS files but leaves user data and applications in place.
questions.trap: Clean install would wipe the user's apps and files. The scenario explicitly says they need to preserve them.

questions.stem: A retiring laptop will be donated to charity. The technician needs to make sure the previous owner's data cannot be recovered. Which format method is BEST?

choices.text: Quick format
Full format
Delete the partitions, then quick format
Re-image the system with the corporate Windows image

questions.explanation: A full format writes zeros across the entire disk, making old data unrecoverable. Quick format only rewrites the file table and leaves the data physically intact.
questions.trap: (c) sounds thorough but quick format still leaves the underlying data on disk. The partition table is gone but forensic tools could still recover content.

questions.stem: Windows 11 install fails on a 5-year-old desktop. PC Health Check reports the CPU is supported and memory is sufficient. What is the most likely blocker?

choices.text: 32-bit Windows version selected
TPM 2.0 missing or Secure Boot not enabled
MBR partition larger than 2 TB
Windows 11 N edition cannot detect media files

questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot. Older hardware often lacks one or both. Since the CPU and RAM passed, that points at the platform security requirements.
questions.trap: (a) is a distractor - there is no 32-bit Windows 11.

questions.stem: A technician needs to install an OS on a workstation with no media drive and no internet access. The workstation is plugged into the corporate LAN. What is the easiest install path?

choices.text: Internet-based installation
External hot-swappable drive with an ISO
PXE network boot to a local install server
Recovery partition

questions.explanation: PXE boots the OS installer from a server on the local network. No local media, no internet required - just the LAN and a PXE server.
questions.trap: (a) requires internet. (d) requires the OS to already be installed and the recovery partition to exist.

questions.stem: Order the following steps for a clean install of Windows from boot media. Place them in the correct order.

items.text: Boot the system from installation media (USB, PXE, ISO, etc.)
Select and partition the target drive (GPT or MBR)
Load any third-party storage / network drivers if prompted
Let the installer copy OS files and reboot

questions.explanation: Third-party drivers must be loaded before partitioning if they are required to see the storage controller. Then partition, format, copy files, and first-boot configuration.
questions.trap: Putting driver loading at the end. If the storage controller is not recognized, the installer can't even see the disk to partition it.

questions.stem: Match each scenario to the correct install type.

pairs.leftText: Push a fully-configured corporate desktop to 500 machines
Move from Windows 10 to Windows 11 keeping apps and files
Donated laptop receives a fresh OS with no previous data
Field tech repairs a corrupted Windows install without touching user data

questions.explanation: Image deployment scales one config to many machines. In-place upgrade preserves user state. Clean install wipes everything. Repair installation fixes OS files without touching user data.

questions.stem: Which statements about GPT are TRUE? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Supports up to 128 partitions per drive
Requires UEFI BIOS to boot from
Limited to a maximum partition size of 2 TB
Does not distinguish between primary and extended partitions

questions.explanation: GPT supports 128 partitions (a), requires UEFI (b), and treats all partitions equally (d). The 2 TB limit is MBR's, not GPT's.
questions.trap: (c) is the MBR limit. Confusing the two limits is a classic trap.
